content.user_title: Guide CTO Strategy and Engineering Decisions
content.value_statement: Engineering leaders need structured ways to assess debt, teams, metrics, and architecture choices. This skill provides calculators, templates, and frameworks for practical CTO decisions.
actual_capabilities: Scores technical debt across architecture, code quality, infrastructure, security, and performance categories.
Estimates hiring needs, role balance, budget, team structure, and scaling risks.
Provides architecture decision record templates, examples, and review checklists.
Defines DORA, quality, team health, and business impact metric frameworks.
Supplies technology evaluation matrices for vendor, build, buy, and open source decisions.
limitations: Calculators use provided inputs and examples, not live repository or financial data.
Recommendations require validation against company context, budget, and regulations.
The skill does not replace legal, finance, compliance, or security review.
Templates and thresholds should be adapted before executive or board use.

use_cases.title: Plan Engineering Growth
use_cases.description: Create a hiring plan, team structure, and budget estimate for a growing engineering organization.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Technical Debt
use_cases.description: Assess debt categories and turn high-risk areas into a practical reduction roadmap.

use_cases.title: Document Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Use ADR templates and evaluation criteria to record major technical decisions clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Technical Debt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a system or product area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use CTO Advisor to assess technical debt for this system. Summarize debt level, top risks, effort, and first actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Team Scaling Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning headcount growth for the next year.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use CTO Advisor to plan engineering team scaling from current headcount to target headcount. Include roles, budget, risks, and timeline.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Use CTO Advisor to draft an ADR for this decision. Include context, options, decision drivers, outcome, and consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Technology Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Use CTO Advisor to compare these technology options. Score technical, business, operational, financial, and risk factors with a recommendation.

output_examples.input: Current team has 25 engineers and needs 75 engineers in four quarters.
output: Recommended plan: hire in quarterly waves with onboarding capacity limits.
Primary risks: rapid growth dilution, management gaps, and recruiting load.
Next actions: prioritize senior hires, add recruiting support, and define team charters.

output_examples.input: A legacy commerce platform has weak tests, manual deployments, and outdated dependencies.
output: Overall debt level: medium-high, with security and infrastructure as top priorities.
Recommended focus: introduce security scanning, improve CI/CD, and define migration milestones.
Effort view: dedicate a fixed sprint capacity before adding major features.

output_examples.input: The team must choose between managed Kubernetes, serverless, and virtual machines.
output: Decision drivers: operational maturity, scalability, reliability, cost, and team expertise.
Suggested path: run a proof of concept and record the outcome in an ADR.
Review needs: security, compliance, migration effort, and exit strategy.

best_practices: Provide realistic team, budget, system, and business context before asking for recommendations.
Review generated plans with engineering, security, finance, and product stakeholders.
Turn outputs into tracked actions with owners, dates, metrics, and review cadence.
anti_patterns: Do not treat default calculator examples as company-specific forecasts.
Do not use a single metric as the only signal for team performance.
Do not choose technology from a scorecard without proof of concept validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with technical debt, team scaling, architecture decisions, engineering metrics, and technology evaluation.

faq.question: Does it inspect my codebase automatically?
faq.answer: No. The included calculators use provided inputs or example data unless you adapt them.

faq.question: Can it create an architecture decision record?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes ADR structure, examples, decision drivers, and review guidance.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for executive judgment?
faq.answer: No. It structures analysis, but leaders must validate facts, risks, and commitments.

faq.question: Does it make vendor decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides criteria, scoring guidance, and templates to support a documented decision.
